newsitem.title: UK: RATE RISE DUE TO "BOTCHED BUDGET" - UK CONSERVATIVES.
newsitem.headline: RATE RISE DUE TO "BOTCHED BUDGET" - UK CONSERVATIVES.

text.p: Britain's opposition Conservatives blamed Thursday's 1/4 point rise in official interest rates on the budget introduced last month by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.

Treasury spokesman Peter Lilley said Brown had talked up the consumer boom, but then done nothing to persuade people to save money they received when a series of mutual building societies transformed themselves into commercial banks.
Lilley said the rise, the fourth in the just under 100 days that the Labour Party has been in power, "is the inevitable result of Gordon Brown's botched budget".

"By using his budget to talk up a consumer boom, but then piling the bulk of his tax increases on pension funds and businesses, and doing nothing to persuade people to save their building society windfalls, Gordon Brown left the Bank (of England) with no option but to push interest rates higher," he said.
He said rising rates and the knowledge that the Bank would err on the side of setting them at higher levels "is pushing the pound ever upward". -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
